title: Waste‐heat‐assisted zero‐liquid‐discharge route selection for flue gas desulfurization wastewater in a 2 × 1000 MW coal‐fired power plant
content:
Abstract

Flue gas desulfurization (FGD) wastewater zero-liquid-discharge (ZLD) is constrained by wastewater salinity, heat-source grade, equipment reliability, residual-solid quality, and plant water balance. This study develops a plant-level route-selection framework for waste-heat-assisted FGD wastewater ZLD and applies it to a design-stage 2 × 1000 MW coal-fired power plant in Zhejiang, China. Two practically feasible routes were evaluated under a unified concentration-and-drying boundary: low-temperature multi-effect flash concentration plus high-temperature bypass flue-gas drying, and air evaporation concentration plus bypass drying. Both routes concentrate 26 t h−1 wastewater to 5.2 t h−1 brine at a concentration ratio of 5, recover approximately 20.8 t h−1 water, and send the residual brine to terminal drying. Multi-effect flash achieved lower total unit costs than air evaporation under both the steam scenario (15.26 vs. 29.70 USD t−1) and the hot-water scenario (8.09 vs. 9.87 USD t−1). The additional investment of multi-effect flash can be offset within approximately 0.28 years under steam heating and 2.03 years under hot-water heating. The framework converts plant-specific engineering constraints into a transferable decision method for large coal-fired units.
